newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Three East Timorese seek refuge in French embassy.
newsitem.headline: Three East Timorese seek refuge in French embassy.

text.p: Three East Timorese men broke into the French embassy in Jakarta early on Wednesday in an apparent asylum bid and to draw international attention to their homeland, witnesses said.
"We are seeking political asylum in Portugal. We feel that our homeland has been taken over by the Indonesian military," said one of the men, who identified himself as Sabino D'Arujo, 26.
"In East Timor we are always chased by the troops of the Suharto regime," said a second man who identified himself as Alberto Da Silva, 23.
The third man was named by his colleagues as Anatolio Francesco Arujo, 21.
The embassy break-in came a day after Indonesia's President Suharto visited East Timor, a former Portuguese colony.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed the territory the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Da Silva said the three men were representatives of East Timor's youths.
"We urge the secretary-general of the United Nations to assign a permanent envoy to be based in East Timor," said Da Silva, reading from a statement that listed nine separate demands.
The men made no mention of East Timorese Bishop Carlos Belo or self-exiled resistance leader Jose Ramos Horta who jointly won the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize last Friday.

The statement asked for a permanent presence from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in three East Timor towns. At present the ICRC has only an office in the territory's capital of Dili.

Da Silva said he and his colleagues wanted the U.N. to supervise a referendum on the future of East Timor, to include jailed resistance leader Xanana Gusmao in any international talks on East Timor, and to investigate all deaths in the territory since 1975.
He said they would ask the French ambassador to urge Paris to support the demands.
The three men said they slipped past security guards to get into the embassy.
The witnesses said one of the men displayed an East Timor flag shortly after the break-in. An Indonesian security guard struggled with the three men for a short while before seizing the flag.
It was the seventh such break-in at the French embassy since November last year.
The spiked iron fence around the embassy was raised by a metre after the last break-in, but the men said they still managed to scale it.
A total of 89 East Timorese have been granted asylum in Portugal since September 1995 after breaking into foreign embassies in Jakarta.
